key_insight: A structured non-physician chart-review enrichment step after automated EHR screening helped narrow a very large sepsis candidate pool into a smaller, more clinically valid cohort for longitudinal research.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve efficiency for sepsis studies by reducing false positives from broad SIRS-based screening while preserving patients most likely to have true sepsis.
method: Automated EHR screen: ≥2 SIRS criteria, microbiologic culture/PCR documentation, and a new antibiotic order.
Non-physician staff performed structured chart review as an enrichment step, then cases were discussed with the primary clinical team.
Enrolled patients were later physician-adjudicated into sepsis, infection without sepsis, undifferentiated critical illness, or non-infectious sepsis mimics.
evidence_signal: Across 4,318 screened patients, 1,220 were flagged and 288 enrolled; among enrolled patients, 73% were adjudicated as sepsis, and in a 9-week sample the enrichment step was associated with higher sepsis-likeness among those not deferred.
watch_item: Because this was a single-center workflow using a specific screening pipeline and a partial 9-week evaluation sample, generalizability and operational burden may differ at other hospitals.
paper_title: Efficiency of a Multi-step Screening and Enrichment Process for Prospective Sepsis Cohort Enrollment
